name: Pyrolytic Fascial Plane Separator PFPS-2 'Peeler'
description:
The PFPS-2 uses a dual-wavelength pyrolytic beam tuned to the specific thermal absorption coefficient of fascial connective tissue — the dense fibrous sheaths that encase every muscle group in the human body. When the beam contacts a target, it selectively superheats the fascial layer without significantly affecting the muscle tissue beneath or the skin above, causing rapid pyrolytic separation: the fascia tears, contracts, and in severe cases vaporizes in localized strips. The result is acute compartment syndrome onset in the affected limb within seconds, accompanied by searing pain as the released pressure differential crushes adjacent nerves and vasculature.

What makes the Peeler distinctively horrifying is its visible effect at high power settings: the skin over the targeted area develops a characteristic rippling, as though something beneath is trying to escape. Operators refer to this as 'the show,' and its psychological impact on bystanders has been documented as a significant secondary effect — witnesses to a Peeler discharge frequently suffer acute stress responses severe enough to require medical intervention. The weapon was originally developed for surgical field applications, intended to replace manual fasciotomy in trauma scenarios, before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS acquired the underlying patent and adapted it.

The weapon platform is compact and pistol-form, fitted with a twin-emitter head that projects the two wavelengths in precise interference pattern. It has a notoriously short effective range — rarely useful beyond 25 meters — but within that envelope it is considered one of the most reliably incapacitating weapons available. Targets struck in the thigh or forearm are typically unable to use the affected limb for days to weeks even with prompt medical care.
legality: Prohibited — classified as a torture instrument under GLMZ Municipal Code 7.4.12
specifications:
effective range: 2–25 meters
beam wavelengths: 3.4 μm and 6.1 μm (tuned to collagen absorption peaks)
time to fascial separation: 1.8–6 seconds depending on tissue depth
incapacitation profile: Acute compartment syndrome, 72+ hour recovery minimum
power source: Pyrolytic induction cell, 14 discharges
weight: 1.4 kg
length: 28 cm
emitter head: Twin-aperture interference projector
targeting assist: Thermal contrast overlay (optional heads-up display sync)
tactical_use: Used in close-quarters scenarios where the operator needs to permanently remove a target's combat capability without killing them — debt enforcement, interrogation preamble, or message-sending contracts. Its short range makes it a contact-to-midrange weapon, typically deployed after a target has been pinned or cornered. Some operators use it in combination with a conventional firearm: the Peeler drops the target's defensive capability in a limb, the firearm handles the follow-through. Organized crime uses it heavily for 'marking' — a single Peeler strike to the dominant hand is a recognizable permanent warning.
cultural_context: The Peeler is associated almost exclusively with the debt-collection and enforcement ecosystem of GLMZ's lower corporate tiers. Carrying one is a statement: the bearer doesn't just want you stopped, they want you to remember it. In certain criminal organizations it is carried exclusively by enforcers who have been granted the explicit authority to maim — a status symbol indicating trust from leadership. Victims of Peeler strikes are identifiable to street medics by their scarring pattern, and within survivor communities the weapon has become a rallying symbol of corporate brutality. There is an underground medical collective called 'The Fascial' that provides free reconstructive care to Peeler victims.
known_users: Debt enforcement arm of the Tsurikov-Maris credit syndicate
Fixer 'Sable Orin' — known for non-lethal but memorable contract resolutions
Black clinic surgeon Dr. Emeka Eze (modified for legitimate fasciotomy use)
story_hooks: A Peeler with a custom serial number is found at a crime scene where the victim — a Helix Biosystems researcher — died of conventional gunshot. Why bring a Peeler if you were going to shoot them anyway? What were they trying to get first?

The Fascial medical collective is being systematically targeted — someone is eliminating the people who document and treat Peeler victims. The party must protect the collective's lead surgeon before a crucial testimony.
A character receives a Peeler strike as a warning from a creditor. The clock is now ticking on both their debt and their limb function — they need a solution to both.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS is lobbying to have the Peeler reclassified from 'torture instrument' to 'less-lethal compliance tool.' Someone is paying the party to make sure that reclassification fails — or succeeds.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist pistol with an oversized, asymmetrical emitter head that dominates the weapon's forward profile. The twin apertures sit recessed in a heat-dispersal collar, giving it the appearance of a predatory insect or surgical instrument retrofitted for violence. Compact and top-heavy.
physical_description.dimensions: 28 cm length overall, 12 cm height including emitter collar, 6 cm width at widest point (emitter head). Twin apertures separated by 3.2 cm centerline.
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and front-loaded — 1.4 kg feels heavier in hand due to the concentrated mass of the emitter assembly. Requires deliberate wrist support, not a casual grip weapon.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten-impregnated polymer frame with steel reinforcement around the grip and trigger assembly. Emitter collar is aerospace-grade aluminum with integrated heat-sink fins.
physical_description.finish: Matte titanium-gray on the frame with anodized black on the grip section. The emitter collar bears a brushed aluminum finish with visible thermal stress marks — faint oxidation streaks and heat-discoloration rings around the apertures.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary slate gray with charcoal black accents on the grip and trigger guard. The emitter apertures have a faint iridescent burn-ring around each — amber to violet from repeated thermal cycling.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with aggressive crosshatch pattern, wrapped at the rear with thin corded synthetic leather for purchase. Deliberately angular, designed for a firm two-handed stance despite its pistol size.
distinctive_features: Twin circular apertures recessed in the emitter collar, separated by interference-pattern alignment ridge
Prominent heat-sink fins running laterally along the emitter assembly
Thermal contrast overlay display window — a small smoked acrylic panel above the iron sights showing target heat signature
Pyrolytic induction cell charge indicator: three discrete LED dots (red-yellow-green) on the left frame, glowing faintly during charge cycle
Engraved serial plate on right grip: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (stylized A with orbital ring) and model designation 'PFPS-2'
Burn-pattern scarring on the emitter collar apertures — evidence of high-power discharge cycles and fascial vaporization
Trigger guard is reinforced and overbuilt, designed for gloved operation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (orbital-A symbol) stamped on the right grip panel below the trigger guard. Model designation 'PEELER' and 'PFPS-2' engraved in small serif type on the left frame above the safety lever. Serial number on the grip backing plate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field weapon with evidence of regular use — micro-scarring around the apertures from thermal cycling, faint carbon discoloration on the emitter collar, grip polymer worn smooth in the operator's contact zones. No visible damage; treated as a precision tool despite its brutal application.

image_prompt: Product photography of a compact, brutalist pyrolytic pistol with twin emitter apertures. Resting on dark matte surface with tactical gloved hand gripping the textured polymer frame. Dramatic side-lighting emphasizing the oversized heat-sink collar and the faint iridescent burn-rings around the apertures. Thermal glow visible in the charge indicator LEDs (amber). Matte titanium-gray finish contrasted against charcoal grip. Background is diffuse dark neo-noir urban aesthetic with faint neon reflection on the weapon's surface. Close enough to see the wear patterns and fascial-tissue scorch marks on the emitter head. Cold, clinical, surgical-weapon vibe. --ar 3:2 --v 6
